notes: manoramaonline.com (Malayala Manorama, India). Result: 2916 unique article URLs covering all 31 days 2026-09-25..2026-10-25 (09-30=110, 10-10=85, 10-20=81), every day 74-113; run 26s warm / ~2.5min cold, 38 requests. ROUTE THAT WORKS: the site-wide chronological firehose listing https://www.manoramaonline.com/news/latest-news.html?page=N (page 1 = 2026-10-25, page 30 = 09-30, page 37 = 09-24), server-rendered AEM, ~248 article hrefs per page from every section (news/latest-news, district-news/*, business/*, global-malayali/*, sports, technology, premium). Article URLs are day permalinks /<section>/<subsection>/YYYY/MM/DD/<slug>.html and the path date IS the outlet's publication date: checked against the page's own JSON-LD "datePublished" on 15 articles across 8 days, 15/15 identical (e.g. .../2026/10/20/stool-used-as-lifeline... -> 2026-10-20T17:15:20+05:30). 15/15 re-fetched samples 200 with 5769-9674 chars of body text, so both parts of the check pass. DEAD ENDS (all probed through polite_fetch): robots.txt is 200 but has NO Sitemap: line (it disallows /rss/, /content/mm/ml/ and /content/mm/mo/, so feeds and the mobile content path are closed); /sitemap.xml is 200 but it is an AEM page dump (a <sitemap> jcr node with 62 child pages), not a sitemap index; every one of the 62 child sitemaps /sitemap/google-news-<section>.xml is HTTP 200 with an EMPTY <urlset> (0 <loc>), so Google-news sitemaps are useless here; /sitemap-index.xml and /news-sitemap.xml are 404; no per-day archive (/news/latest-news/2026/10/20.html, /archive/2026/10/20.html both 404); /news/latest-news.html (no ?page) works but only carries the last day, which is why paging is needed. STYLE/DATE CHOICE: dates come only from the URL day permalink, corroborated by datePublished, never from a crawl date; sections that are link farms rather than articles (web-stories, kerala-lottery-results) are filtered out to keep the body-text requirement safe; URLs are deduped by path (each card appears ~2x in the markup) and written URL<TAB>YYYY-MM-DD sorted by date then URL. The listing repeats 6 pinned links dated today on every page, so the loop stops when the page's second-newest date walks past the window start, not when the newest does.
